claims.text: Mechanical-property differences among equiatomic FCC Cr-Mn-Fe-Co-Ni-based alloys arise from composition-dependent local lattice distortions.
Mean-square atomic displacement (MSAD) is an indicator of composition-dependent local lattice distortion.
Local lattice distortions create composition-dependent dislocation glide-resistance landscapes.
Higher MSAD raises the extrapolated 0 K critical resolved shear stress through solid-solution strengthening.
Increased Mn and Fe content promotes dynamic solute pinning at elevated temperatures.
Dynamic pinning by Mn- and Fe-rich solutes produces the Portevin-Le Chatelier effect through elastic solute-dislocation interactions.
Below approximately 60–77 K, inertial dislocation motion becomes an operative deformation mechanism.
Dynamic solute pinning becomes operative at approximately 673 K and above.
At cryogenic temperatures, reduced phonon drag allows thermally activated glide to be strongly affected by solid-solution obstacles modulated by local lattice distortion.
At approximately 673–873 K and above, diffusible Mn- and Fe-rich solutes form Cottrell-type atmospheres around dislocations.
Cottrell-type solute atmospheres elastically pin dislocations and lead to serrated flow.
Relative to the quinary alloy, lower-Cr quaternary and ternary alloys will have lower average MSAD.
Relative to the quinary alloy, lower-Cr quaternary and ternary alloys will exhibit lower extrapolated 0 K CRSS.
Relative to the quinary alloy, lower-Cr quaternary and ternary alloys will exhibit a smaller PL-related CRSS increment at high temperature.
Alloys with relatively higher Mn and Fe content will exhibit a more pronounced PL strengthening increment.
The proposed relationships apply to equiatomic, single-phase FCC Cr-Mn-Fe-Co-Ni-based concentrated solid solutions tested as [1̄23]-oriented bulk single crystals in compression.
Suzuki segregation may affect some compositions, including CrFeNi.

contradictions.description: The conditions state that measurements focus outside both the inertial regime and the high-temperature diffusion/PL-active regime, while the mechanism, predictions, and boundary explicitly rely on observations in the PL-active regime at approximately 673 K and above.

The prediction distinguishes outcomes by Cr, Mn, and Fe content, but the falsification rule broadly requires quaternary and ternary alloys to show systematically lower 0 K CRSS and diminished PL increments. Equiatomic subsets retaining Cr, Mn, or Fe can have higher atomic fractions of those elements than the quinary alloy, so the blanket falsification criterion does not follow from the composition-specific predictions.

The high-temperature PL increment is mechanistically attributed to Mn and Fe, yet one prediction links a diminished PL increment to reduced Cr/MSAD. No explicit connection is supplied between Cr-dependent MSAD and the Mn/Fe-controlled PL increment.
